narrative.intro: Corecivic obligated $77M in federal contracts in FY2027 to date, spread across 9 awards with an average award size of $8.6M. Corecivic obligations fell 83.1% year over year. Corecivic has a multi-year history of larger obligations: FY22 obligations were $288M, FY23 obligations were $253M, FY24 obligations were $271M, FY25 obligations were $396M, and FY26 obligations were $455M. Corecivic receives the largest share of FY2027 to-date obligations from the Department of Homeland Security, which obligated $49.8M, followed by the Department of Justice, which obligated $27.2M. Corecivic sells services primarily in Security Guards and Patrol Services, which accounted for $53.2M in FY2027 to date, and in Other Residential Care Facilities, which accounted for $18.5M, plus Other Justice, Public Order, and Safety Activities at $5.3M. Current-year totals are partial and represent fiscal year to date obligations, while some tables report award-value figures as total contract values.

sections.heading: How did Corecivic's FY2027 obligations compare with prior years?
sections.body: Corecivic obligated $77M in FY2027 to date. Corecivic obligations fell 83.1% year over year. Corecivic obligations were $455M in FY26 and trended lower from FY25 through FY23 before that, with FY25 at $396M, FY24 at $271M, FY23 at $253M, and FY22 at $288M.

sections.heading: Who are Corecivic's main federal customers and what do they buy?
sections.body: The Department of Homeland Security obligated $49.8M in FY2027 to date and the Department of Justice obligated $27.2M. Corecivic sells Security Guards and Patrol Services, which accounted for $53.2M in FY2027 to date, Other Residential Care Facilities at $18.5M, and Other Justice, Public Order, and Safety Activities at $5.3M.

faq.q: How much does Corecivic make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Corecivic obligated $77M in federal contract obligations in FY2027 to date. Corecivic has 9 awards in FY2027 to date with an average award size of $8.6M, and obligations fell 83.1% year over year compared with the prior fiscal year.
The Department of Homeland Security obligated $49.8M from Corecivic in FY2027 to date. The Department of Justice obligated $27.2M from Corecivic in FY2027 to date.

faq.q: What does Corecivic sell to the government?
faq.a: Corecivic sells Security Guards and Patrol Services, Other Residential Care Facilities, and Other Justice, Public Order, and Safety Activities to the federal government. Security Guards and Patrol Services accounted for $53.2M, Other Residential Care Facilities accounted for $18.5M, and Other Justice, Public Order, and Safety Activities accounted for $5.3M in FY2027 to date.

faq.q: Which Corecivic contracts are expiring soon?
faq.a: This summary does not list specific expiring-contract figures. The available tables show award-value figures and obligations but do not include a separate list of expiring contracts in the presented figures.
